I found the two real candidate events in **Codeunit 80 "Sales-Post"** (`Base Application/Sales/Posting/SalesPost.Codeunit.al` in the w1-28 base app). Here's what the actual source shows:

## Candidate 1: `OnBeforePostSalesDoc` — line ~8977

Fires at the very first line of `RunWithCheck`, which is what `OnRun` calls to kick off posting:

```al
trigger OnRun()                                    // line 110
begin
    RunWithCheck(Rec);
end;

internal procedure RunWithCheck(var SalesHeader2: Record "Sales Header")
var
    ...
begin
    SequenceNoMgt.SetPreviewMode(PreviewMode);
    IsHandled := false;
    OnBeforePostSalesDoc(SalesHeader2, SuppressCommit, PreviewMode, HideProgressWindow, IsHandled, CalledBy);
    if IsHandled then
        exit;

    GetSalesHeader(SalesHeader2);   // <-- everything else happens after this
    ...
```

Parameters (verified from the call site): `var SalesHeader2`, `SuppressCommit`, `PreviewMode`, `var HideProgressWindow`, `var IsHandled`, `CalledBy`.

This is the earliest possible hook — it fires **before** BC even re-fetches/locks the header, before the release-status check, before dimension/no-series checks, before any sales lines are touched. Nothing has been written yet. Because `IsHandled` is a `var` parameter, setting it `true` skips the entire rest of posting — but for validation you don't need that; you just run your check and call `Error()`, which aborts cleanly with zero side effects since nothing has happened yet.

## Candidate 2: `OnBeforePostCommitSalesDoc` — line ~9023

Declared immediately after the first event in the same file, but positioned (per its name and location relative to `FinalizePosting`) to fire right before the final `Commit()` — i.e. **after** shipment/invoice/credit memo headers, item ledger entries, and G/L entries have all already been created in the (uncommitted) transaction. I confirmed the actual `Commit()` call in `FinalizePosting` (part 5/5):

```al
if not (InvtPickPutaway or SuppressCommit or PreviewMode) then
    Commit();
```

I could not pull the exact call-site line for `OnBeforePostCommitSalesDoc` through the search tool (the file is huge and this chunk didn't surface), so treat its exact wiring as inferred-from-naming-and-position rather than fully verified — but functionally it's a late-stage hook, not an early-validation one.

## Execution order & recommendation

`OnBeforePostSalesDoc` → [all checks, all line posting, all ledger entry creation, `FinalizePosting`] → `OnBeforePostCommitSalesDoc` → `Commit()`

This isn't ambiguous the way the events-scenario often is — the two events sit at opposite ends of the same posting run, so the choice comes down to intent:

- **Use `OnBeforePostSalesDoc`** if you want to *block* posting outright (e.g. "customer's credit hold flag isn't set" or "a required field on the header isn't filled"). It's cheap to fail fast here since nothing has run yet.
- **`OnBeforePostCommitSalesDoc`** would only make sense if your validation genuinely needs to inspect the *results* of posting (e.g. the generated invoice/shipment numbers or created ledger entries) before allowing the commit — that's a much rarer case, and erroring here still rolls back cleanly, it's just wasted work getting there.

For "custom validation right before a sales order gets posted" as you phrased it, **`OnBeforePostSalesDoc` is the right one** — it's the standard subscription point for this exact purpose in real AL extensions.
